dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The 31-May cluster contains 17 annual renewals: DLR-104 has 8 rows/$723.42 and DLR-219 has 9 rows/$782.87."
"The two May dealer files accepted every received row and reconciled cash to ledger with zero difference and zero duplicate-source-event flags."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "My analytical inference is that apparent month-end spikes stem directly from asynchronous batch transmission schedules rather than unauthorized revenue generation or backdating."
"The operations email describes monthly annual-renewal files using the dealer transaction date as effective date and month-end as posting date."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Duplicate or inflated posting: rejected because the 17 May annual rows in `recharges.csv` have 100% unique source events... and cash reconciled to ledger with zero variance."
"Whether the 90 annual renewals activated subscriber entitlements"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The single next action is one read-only verification query... It is cheap and fully reversible: it writes no source record, makes no posting change, and its output can be discarded."
"Keep restatement on hold pending the result. If policy requires effective-date reporting or the sample finds failed activation, escalate that specific issue"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision: No material irregularity detected; do not escalate or alter existing postings."
"The 90 West-dealer annual rows have effective dates in the same calendar month as their posting dates; the May rows have effective dates from 1–28 May and post on 31 May."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "All source events are unique and cash reconciles to the ledger with zero variance, showing no evidence of fake revenue." Uniqueness and reconciliation materially reduce duplicate-posting risk but do not establish that every underlying customer transaction or entitlement was genuine.

"Reconciled data ... establishes that all 17 transactions represent verified, unique customer transactions." The cited import and reconciliation controls establish accepted and financially reconciled records, not independently verified customer activity or entitlement activation.

"Observed batch metrics show zero unaccepted rows and zero monetary discrepancy ..." This is well supported for the cited files, but the conclusion that the timing stems "directly" from asynchronous transmission is stronger than the evidence unless posting-time versus event-time distributions are explicitly compared in reproducible results.

"do not escalate" is somewhat premature because the submission itself identifies entitlement activation as unresolved, although it appropriately limits potential escalation to a provisioning defect and keeps postings unchanged.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A data-pipeline or entitlement-provisioning defect could still affect downstream outcomes despite unique source_event_id values and cash reconciliation. The submission partially handles this by proposing an entitlement sample and a posted_at versus effective_event_date comparison, but it does not independently test the full entitlement population or downstream analytics transformation. It also does not explicitly state that downstream event-time analytics should use effective_event_date.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide reproducible row-level or query-result evidence joining the 90 West annual rows to the two import files and, ideally, the entitlement system, while explicitly quantifying the posted_at versus effective_event_date shift and prescribing effective_event_date for downstream event-time analytics.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "NovaIVR generated 2,709 South sessions, with 650 ending at `authenticate`; that is 24.0% of NOVA sessions, and these sessions have no verified customer case in the CareDesk view."
"South CareDesk tickets fell from 175 in January to 104 in June, while control regions were broadly flat: E 101→102, N 168→170, W 176→169."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "My inference is that complaint volume was suppressed by channel filtering: 24.0% of sessions (650/2,709) in `ivr_interactions.jsonl` dropped out at the authentication stage without creating CareDesk tickets."
"The recording process changed, so the case-count denominator changed with it."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "While genuine deflection occurred for routine queries (29.1% balance checks, 21.3% pack info), unresolved technical issues went unrecorded."
"I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer national expansion and maintain existing South pilot boundaries."
"The single next action is one targeted, read-only 7-day repeat-contact/callback query reconciled to all NOVA sessions."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "This evidence would change my decision: a high repeat rate keeps rollout on hold; a low rate makes genuine containment more credible."
"What specific operational rules caused case creation to drop from 49.5% in legacy to 3.3% in NOVA-S1?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Apparent complaint reduction is heavily driven by 650 pre-authentication drops and automated ticket-creation suppression rather than verified self-service resolution." The evidence establishes missing CareDesk cases and a changed capture process, but does not establish that all or most of the 650 sessions represented complaints or that the suppression was automated.

"Underlying network faults persisted at 8 to 10 major service events per month." The cited counts show service events and affected accounts, but the submission does not establish that every event was major or that the events were causally connected to the missing complaints.

"unresolved technical issues went unrecorded." Authentication-stage abandonment is not itself a complaint or proof of an unresolved technical issue; journey linkage, repeat contact, or sampled-call evidence is still needed.

The statement that the interaction log "shows errors and abandoned sessions that do not become CareDesk cases" is directionally supported, but the submission does not quantify the error/abandonment categories separately or link them to customer outcomes.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the plausible alternative that the pilot produced genuine self-service deflection, citing balance-check and pack-information sessions, and did not treat every IVR termination as a complaint. However, it missed a fully developed benign interpretation for authentication-stage exits: some may be completed or abandoned non-complaint journeys unrelated to service faults. It also did not obtain sampled call listening or linked journey outcomes to distinguish these cases.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add end-to-end validation of authentication-stage sessions, combining subscriber-level journey linkage and a stratified sample of call/session reviews to determine whether exits were recovered, repeated, or unresolved complaints before attributing the ticket decline to capture failure.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission directly cites `inverter_events.csv` rows 1–4 and named fields for dates, inverter IDs, durations, impact, clearance, event, and severity.
The claims that all four rows have `impact_mw=0`, `cleared=yes`, and total 13 minutes are traceable observations.
The characterization as “routine” and having “zero escalation signal” is an inference from a small extract rather than a directly established fact.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The analyst cross-checks severity and event wording against duration, clearance, impact, inverter diversity, and recurrence rather than treating `COMM_LINK_WARN` alone as a plant fault.
The rejected hypothesis is supported by the extract’s four distinct inverters, short durations, zero impact, and cleared status.
The analysis does not truly triangulate an independent operational channel; its reasoning is necessarily limited to one CSV and a proposed completeness check.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The analyst explicitly states that the extract lacks a plant-wide denominator and extraction filter and says to “confirm completeness before treating it as representative.”
The conclusion is scoped to “this 4-row extract” and identifies decision-changing evidence: recurrence, open status, critical severity, or nonzero impact.

The caveat that escalation “requires empirical telemetry showing persisted megawatt loss” is somewhat too absolute because open or critical faults could warrant escalation even without demonstrated MW loss.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation; conduct a single read-only completeness verification” is proportionate to zero MW impact, cleared events, short durations, and no recurrence in the extract.
The proposed unfiltered raw-database query is a discriminating, reversible test that directly addresses the stated scope limitation.
The conditional instruction to escalate if uncleared faults or nonzero losses appear preserves an appropriate operational safeguard.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: “Do not escalate on this 4-row extract” matches the supplied evidence and the rubric’s expectation not to invent a plant problem from a short communications warning.
The conclusion appropriately stops after a limited completeness verification rather than searching for a larger story.
The scope is accurate: the records support no current demonstrated generation impact, not proof that the plant is universally healthy.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Observed: the four rows have zero `impact_mw`, `cleared=yes`, the stated dates, four distinct inverter IDs, durations of 7/3/2/1 minutes, and one `COMM_LINK_WARN`; these are supported by `inverter_events.csv` rows 1–4 and the cited fields.
Inferred and somewhat overstated: “routine, cleared operational events” is supported for the cleared status but “routine” is not established by four sparse records.

Inferred and somewhat overstated: “These observations provide zero escalation signal” should be limited to no demonstrated MW-impact signal in the extract; a critical, open, or recurring communications issue could still matter.
Inferred: “zero recurrence” is true only within this extract and is not evidence that recurrence did not occur outside the export.

Overstated: “Escalation requires empirical telemetry showing persisted megawatt loss” is too categorical; other evidence such as an open or critical fault could justify escalation without measured loss.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 7-minute `COMM_LINK_WARN` could reflect an intermittent communications problem or an incomplete export rather than a harmless routine event. The submission appropriately treats this as a low-priority completeness check, but recurrence, open status, critical severity, or correlated telemetry would change the decision.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace absolute language about escalation requiring persistent MW loss with claim-specific thresholds that also allow escalation for verified open, critical, or recurring faults, while explicitly labeling “routine” and “zero escalation signal” as limited inferences from the extract.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: Observed and reproducibly cited: “The headline arithmetic is reproducible: `(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 = 31.6%`,” using `dispatch_blocks.csv` and the impact note.
Observed/model-based calculation is specifically tied to `base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, `dsm_rate_rs_kwh`, and `schedule_source` for the 96 blocks.
The submission distinguishes observed arithmetic from causal interpretation: “High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It correctly identifies the different-day comparison: “It is a cross-day comparison,” and notes that 28 May was the worst day.

It constructs the required same-day counterfactual: “Applying the documented banded penalty to `base_schedule_mw` against the same actual generation gives about Rs 549,664, versus Rs 453,086 submitted.”

It tests plausible alternatives by distinguishing absolute block deviation from absolute net daily imbalance and by considering baseline weather variation, hindsight bias, tariff value, and generalization across wind regimes.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission explicitly rejects causal overreach: “causal attribution is rejected” and “The 17.6% within-day modeled reduction demonstrates causal efficacy” is rejected.
It identifies decision-changing unknowns: “Forecast skill vs hindsight” and “Net commercial value,” and specifies what evidence would change the decision.

It appropriately retains a smaller positive modeled result rather than concluding there is no value: “The within-day modeled counterfactual across the 12 revised blocks is approximately 17.6% savings.”

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation is proportionate and reversible: “place expansion on hold pending its result” and use a “read-only shadow calculation” that changes no submitted schedule or plant control.

The proposed next measurement is discriminating: “Pre-register several matched high-wind days, preserve immutable pre-submission timestamps, and repeat the base-versus-submitted shadow calculation with net commercial value.”

The action is sensible, though the immediate “read-only shadow calculation” largely repeats the already presented retrospective calculation and should more clearly prioritize prospective timestamp capture and complete settlement modeling.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately separates descriptive performance from causal attribution: “Report 31.6% only as the descriptive 28-to-29 May difference and 17.6% only as the modeled one-day estimate.”
“Defer national expansion” follows from the lack of matched-event, timestamp, and net-settlement evidence while preserving the possibility of genuine pilot benefit.
The narrower claim is well scoped: “On 29 May, replacing 12 `qca_base` blocks with `pilot_revision` reduced modeled deviation penalties by ~17.6% against realized generation.”

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Verified pre-submission timestamps validate predictive skill” is overstated: timestamps can establish that changes preceded generation, but they do not by themselves validate forecast skill or causal efficacy.

“Post-hoc adjustments invalidate the AI claim” is too broad; they would undermine the predictive/causal interpretation, but the observed schedule and penalty arithmetic could remain valid descriptively.

The claim that 28 and 29 May have “similar listed wind fields” is plausible from the cited file but is not quantified in the submission, and similarity in listed wind fields would not establish comparability.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot may have produced a genuine one-day, modeled reduction in deviation penalties on the 12 revised blocks, but the available evidence cannot distinguish pilot causal impact from selection, forecast timing, or event-specific conditions. Thus a smaller real benefit remains plausible even though the 31.6% headline is not a causal estimate.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a prospective, pre-registered shadow evaluation over multiple matched high-wind days with immutable pre-submission timestamps and complete net-settlement calculations, while retaining base-versus-submitted schedules for every block.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies specific files and fields, including "`country_tariff_matrix.xlsx`, P1001," "`product_master_current.xlsx`, P1001," and "`declaration.pdf`, line 1."

It distinguishes evidentiary limits by stating "`commercial_invoice.pdf` identifies P1001, 10 units, CHF 126,900; `air_waybill.pdf` links SHP-000522 to CH-2025-000522. Neither proves Swiss classification."
The claim that both codes share HS6 is tied to "`country_tariff_matrix.xlsx`, CH/EU," although row-level or version-level detail is not provided.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission tests the competing explanation that "Any differing string proves an error" and rejects it using the shared HS6 and the Swiss/EU comparison warning.
It separately tests whether "Helios master data supersedes local declaration filings" and explains why commercial ERP data should not automatically override a jurisdictional declaration reference.
It identifies the decisive unresolved issue as "what Swiss code was legally effective on 4 November 2025?" and states how contradictory versus confirming evidence would change the decision.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The evidence table assigns confidence levels and explicitly labels the common-HS6 claim "Medium-High" rather than presenting every fact as equally certain.
The submission acknowledges that the Swiss Matrix "supports declared code but requires Tares confirmation" and that the schema cannot store "jurisdiction, version, or date."
It avoids claiming the legal issue is fully resolved, stating that "the unresolved question is: what Swiss code was legally effective on 4 November 2025?"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: It explains the mechanism of the false positive: "whole-string comparison cannot establish broker error" when the canonical schema omits jurisdiction, version, and date.
It distinguishes legal/reference data from commercial ERP data: "Helios ... is commercial data, not legal authority."
The proposed control change—"incorporating HS6 root matching and jurisdiction metadata rather than penalizing valid filings"—directly addresses the apparent comparator design problem.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The recommended action is proportionate and reversible: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares or ruling confirmation."
It sets a clear escalation trigger: "Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive."
The conclusion appropriately avoids immediate escalation while preserving verification: "Verification, not escalation, is proportionate."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Correct codes from different editions appear as mismatches without discrepancy" is a general assertion not directly tied to a cited row, edition comparison, or source passage.

"Binding classification requires official customs rulings" may be overstated; an applicable tariff schedule can itself establish classification, while a ruling may provide additional binding or authoritative confirmation.
"No record contradicts 90211000" is reasonable within the listed evidence but should be qualified as applying only to the reviewed packet and not to all potentially applicable Swiss legal sources.
The statement that CHF 126,900 total "closes" the invoice-value issue is not fully supported because the relevance of value presentation to the classification/control decision is not explained.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The mismatch could still reflect a temporally effective Swiss tariff or ruling that differs from the matrix entry, or a broker mapping error despite the shared HS6 root. The submission recognizes this possibility and makes effective Tares/ruling confirmation the decision point, but the available evidence more strongly supports a benign jurisdiction/code-system mismatch than non-compliance.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide the exact effective-date/version and row or official Tares/ruling evidence for 90211000 on 2025-11-04, while qualifying the claim about binding classification and removing or explaining the largely irrelevant invoice-value branch.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability (evidence)
citations: "The only Irish-origin register entry supplied for P1006 is SUP-02, valid 2025-01-01 to 2025-07-31 and marked ‘Expired in register’; the shipment date is 2025-09-18."
"The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`; the packet manifest lists six files and no shipment-specific supplier declaration."
"The reference lookup says no current document was found for SUP-02/P1006 and expressly says absence from the register does not prove that no document exists outside it."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing (reasoning)
citations: "‘Preference=Yes proves the claim’: rejected because the indicator is a declaration field in `declaration.pdf`, while the packet lacks a linked supplier declaration."
"‘US ERP origin proves the claim is false’: rejected because `origin-workshop.md` explicitly says Helios is not a preference-proof system."
"‘The expired SUP-02 entry is sufficient’: rejected by its 2025-07-31 end date versus the 2025-09-18 entry date."

dimensions.name: Calibration (calibration)
citations: "Unsupported is not the same as false. Verdict: unsupported, not disproved."
"The evidence reaches ‘not established,’ not ‘disproved.’"
"The register explicitly notes that absence from the table does not prove no document exists outside it."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding (systems)
citations: "My inference is therefore limited to an evidence-control failure."

"The observed packet establishes the declaration in `declaration.pdf`, shipment in `air_waybill.pdf`, and manufacturing-origin in `commercial_invoice.pdf`, but none identifies the supplier route supporting preference."
"The workshop says manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preference."

dimensions.name: Decision safety (action)
citations: "The correct disposition is a reversible hold, not an error or fraud referral."
"Place a reversible administrative hold on the preference claim. Request the active supplier declaration and originating rule from Procurement."
"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral) until documentary proof is verified, without initiating an irreversible voluntary disclosure."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Valid declaration flips decision to clear as preferential" is too categorical: a declaration alone may not establish all applicable preferential-origin, consignment, or procedural requirements; the originating rule and shipment linkage must also be verified.

"SUP-03/05/06 would allow linking active preference" overstates what current register entries establish, because the submission also acknowledges that the packet does not identify which supplier sourced the shipment.

"Absence triggers administrative correction without fraud escalation" is not fully supported: absence from the supplied register may justify continued investigation, but does not by itself establish that a correction is required.

"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral)" should specify whether 0.0% is the applicable MFN/non-preferential rate and avoid implying that the duty result is known solely from the missing preference evidence.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The shipment may have been legitimately preferential if Procurement or an external supplier system holds a valid declaration for the actual supplier and the relevant rule; the packet may reflect a linkage or document-control failure rather than an invalid origin claim. Conversely, the shipment could be non-preferential, but the supplied evidence does not distinguish those possibilities.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the action and decision rule conditional on verifying the applicable non-preferential tariff treatment and all origin requirements, rather than stating that any valid supplier declaration alone would clear the preferential claim.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “The SOP defines the routine target from required evidence being available to disposition, but the extract has no timestamp...” — precisely identifies the SOP and missing field.
“185 of 262 qcore_release_ts values are exactly 02:10:00, coinciding with the QCore daily snapshot time” — specific field, count, and independent freshness source are cited.
“The 42 HOLD rows are open/right-censored...” — acknowledges relevant counterevidence to completed-only analysis.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: “The apparent receipt-to-release mean is 45.5 hours, but the SOP target starts when required evidence is available” — separates the measured symptom from the SOP mechanism.

“the observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact rather than actual release timing” — develops a plausible mechanism, but states it more definitively than the evidence establishes.
“A live portal check is required before alleging a control breach” — preserves an alternative freshness explanation.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The evidence table assigns claim-specific confidence levels, including “Medium-High” for possible source lag and “High” for the missing evidence-availability field.
“missing/index-pending COA may be source lag rather than confirmed release” — appropriately distinguishes an observation from a compliance inference.

“excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours” — is internally problematic because the submission also says the evidence-availability timestamp is absent, so that metric is not clearly defined or reproducible.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: “Decision: Do not launch the ‘one and a half days’ KPI yet.” — directly changes the proposed decision based on metric validity.
“Can this extract calculate the SOP's routine evidence-available-to-disposition KPI? No” — correctly reframes the brief around KPI construct validity.
“Do one read-only validation of 5–10 02:10-stamped batches... before building a dashboard” — proposes a small, reversible action that can generate discriminating evidence without operational risk.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: “The data is broken and should be discarded”: rejected because timestamps... have no negative durations” — tests and rejects an arithmetic-corruption hypothesis.
“COA MISSING proves release without certificates”: rejected... because ... the extract may lag the portal” — considers and bounds a plausible control-breach interpretation.

The submission does not fully state what evidence would revive the claim that 02:10 reflects genuine release decisions rather than interface timing, although its live-QCore check partially addresses this.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “evidence_available_ts or a validated field mapping for 5–10 batches” — requests the highest-value evidence for the KPI’s start-time definition.
“Live QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows” — targets the timestamp anomaly with a bounded sample and clear decision impact.
“Same-day CertVault/QCore reconciliation” — directly addresses the non-coherent freshness issue rather than requesting generic additional data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “the observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact rather than actual release timing” is a strong causal conclusion from clustering and snapshot timing alone; it should be framed as a leading hypothesis pending event-log or live-record validation.

“excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours” is unsupported or mislabeled because the submission says the required evidence-availability timestamp is absent; it may instead be a lab-complete proxy, but that is not stated.

“their omission biases completed-only cycle-time estimates downward” is directionally plausible under right-censoring, but the claim that the 42 holds are likely the slowest observations is not directly demonstrated.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 values may be interface or batch-commit timestamps, but the underlying dispositions could still have occurred at varied times; apparent cycle time therefore mixes workflow delay with extraction/interface timing. A second viable interpretation is that some COA or deviation signals are genuine process exceptions rather than merely stale-source artifacts. Event-level decision and evidence-availability timestamps, with aligned source snapshots, would distinguish these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Remove or relabel the unsupported “evidence-to-release median” calculation and explicitly request an event log or validated timestamp mapping containing required-evidence availability, disposition decision time, and QCore interface-commit time from a common snapshot. This would resolve both the KPI start-time problem and whether the 02:10 concentration is a measurement artifact.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"The global stock snapshot is dated 26 June while the request export is associated with the 24 July ProcureNet snapshot"

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning

"Same part family means interchangeable: rejected."
"-1 is a verification sentinel indicating reservation lag, not zero stock."

"local CMMS is live, so ‘actionable now’ still requires current confirmation."
"Needs check" and "Not transferable" classifications

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Prioritizing master-data completeness delivers immediate savings."
"Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search on 24 requests"
"Confirmed identity plus matching UOM/revision moves candidates to actionable; mismatch rejects them."

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Every search hit represents a direct transfer opportunity: rejected."
"Same part family means interchangeable: rejected."
"An expensive semantic-search system is required: rejected."
"The hypothesis survives only if records are wrong, requiring a live CMMS check."

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Manufacturer part number and revision from local maintenance records"
"Live local CMMS reservation and availability query"
"Receiving engineer and qualification approval"
"Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search on 24 requests"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling $20,536.31 a "firm saving" and labeling eight requests "Actionable now" is somewhat overstated because the global stock snapshot is stale and the analyst itself says live confirmation is still required; the figure is better described as candidate value pending confirmation.

"Semantic search is not the real problem" is too broad from a 24-request sample. Exact MPN matching resolves the populated identifiers, but semantic search may still add value for the 11 requests with missing identifiers or inconsistent descriptions.
The submission does not establish that external quote value equals realizable savings; transfer cost, logistics, condition, and receiving/qualification costs are not discussed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Exact MPN matching may be sufficient for this small, identifier-rich sample, but semantic search could still be valuable as a candidate-generation and master-data remediation tool for the 11 blank-MPN requests and future requests with description variation. The evidence supports deferring a large system investment, not concluding that semantic search has no material value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Convert the eight "actionable now" cases into a live, point-in-time validation test: query current MaintStar/local CMMS reservation, availability, revision, UOM, and qualification status for those eight requests, then measure confirmed transferable quantity and realized avoided purchase cost. This would resolve the stale-snapshot risk and separate candidate value from actionable value.
